resource.name: aws_lightsail_key_pair
resource.description: Provides a Lightsail Key Pair, for use with Lightsail Instances. These key pairs are separate from EC2 Key Pairs, and must be created or imported for use with Lightsail. Lightsail is currently only supported in a limited number of AWS Regions, please see "Regions and Availability Zones in Amazon Lightsail" for more details
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_lightsail_key_pair` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of SSH key pairs specifically for Amazon Lightsail instances, distinct from EC2 key pairs. It is commonly used to securely configure access to Lightsail virtual servers, supporting scenarios like deploying lightweight applications, websites, or development environments in Lightsail-supported AWS regions. Users can import existing keys or generate new ones, facilitating lifecycle management and secure authentication for Lightsail-based infrastructure.

examples.title: Create New Key Pair
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to create a new AWS Lightsail key pair using the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource, specifying the `name` argument to define the key pair's identifier. This example is ideal for users looking to set up SSH key pairs for secure access to Lightsail instances."

examples.title: Create New Key Pair with PGP Encrypted Private Key
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to create an AWS Lightsail key pair with a PGP-encrypted private key using the `pgp_key` argument, enabling secure storage and retrieval of the private key. This example highlights the integration of Keybase for managing PGP keys in Terraform configurations."

examples.title: Existing Public Key Import
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to import an existing public SSH key into AWS Lightsail using the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource. It highlights the use of the `public_key` argument to specify the path to a local public key file, enabling secure access to Lightsail instances with pre-existing SSH credentials.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the key pair, typically used to reference or manage the resource programmatically within Terraform configurations. Setting this argument can help ensure consistent tracking and retrieval of the key pair, aligning with common goals like resource organization and automation.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the Lightsail Key Pair. If omitted, a unique name will be generated by Terraform
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource allows users to define a custom, human-readable identifier for the Lightsail Key Pair, facilitating easier management and organization of key pairs within their infrastructure. If omitted, Terraform generates a unique name automatically, making this argument useful for aligning key pair naming conventions with project or environment-specific requirements.

arguments.name: name_prefix
arguments.llm_summary: The `name_prefix` argument for the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource allows users to define a prefix for the name of the Lightsail key pair, enabling automatic generation of a unique name with the specified prefix. This is useful for creating key pairs with consistent naming conventions across environments or projects while avoiding name conflicts.

arguments.name: pgp_key
arguments.description: – (Optional) An optional PGP key to encrypt the resulting private key material. Only used when creating a new key pair
arguments.llm_summary: The `pgp_key` argument in the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource allows users to specify a PGP public key for encrypting the private key material generated during the creation of a new key pair. This ensures secure handling of sensitive key data, aligning with best practices for encryption and data protection in cloud environments.

arguments.name: public_key
arguments.description: (Required) The public key material. This public key will be imported into Lightsail
arguments.llm_summary: The `public_key` argument in the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource allows users to specify the public key material to be imported into AWS Lightsail, enabling secure SSH access to Lightsail instances. By defining this argument, users can configure authentication for managing instances, aligning with common goals of establishing secure and controlled access to cloud resources.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the collection. To create a key-only tag, use an empty string as the value. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level. a PGP key is not required, however it is strongly encouraged. Without a PGP key, the private key material will be stored in state unencrypted.pgp_key is ignored if public_key is supplied.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource allows users to assign metadata in the form of key-value pairs to the key pair, enabling organization, categorization, or identification of the resource within AWS. This supports common user goals like tagging for cost allocation, environment labeling, or resource grouping, and can override provider-level default tags if matching keys are defined.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_lightsail_key_pair` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are applied to the Lightsail key pair for organizational, categorization, or cost allocation purposes. By setting this argument, users can ensure consistent tagging across resources, enabling streamlined resource management, tracking, and integration with AWS billing and reporting tools.

attributes.name: arn
attributes.description: The ARN of the Lightsail key pair.

attributes.name: encrypted_fingerprint
attributes.description: The MD5 public key fingerprint for the encrypted private key.

attributes.name: fingerprint
attributes.description: The MD5 public key fingerprint as specified in section 4 of RFC 4716.

attributes.name: private_key
attributes.description: the private key, base64 encoded. This is only populated when creating a new key, and when no `pgp_key` is provided.
